label: Events
description: Waits for events and starts tasks. Run as one task named `events` per project, and one in Shared, whenever this workflow has at least one automation; it runs unattended and may only start tasks and post notices. An automation is a named state-level transition into an `"async": true` child: `{ "name": "push_main", "when": "on_event('git.push', { branch: 'main' })", "to": "push_main", "inputs": { "event": ".event" } }` with the child `"push_main": { "async": true }`, whose state is the file beside this one, `system/events/push_main` — found through the layers like any state, so a project's own copy of that one file changes that automation for that project alone. That state takes the event (`"inputs": { "event": { "schema": {}, "optional": true } }`) and its steps are ONE operation list, run in order: `"operation": [ { "function": "start_task", "args": { "workflow": "feature/review", "inputs": { "issue": { "$binding": { "$expr": ".inputs.event.payload.commits[0].message" } } } } }, { "function": "notify", "args": { "text": "started a review" } } ]`. `start_task` starts the task as this state's child (the events task lists it) unless `"top_level": true`. Shared's copy is `{ "$ref": "$SYSTEM/workflows/system/events", "transitions": [ … ], "children": { … } }`, both lists spelled out. A project's copy keeps Shared's automations: `{ "$ref": "$BASE/workflows/system/events", "transitions": [ …its own lines, { "$ref": "...filter($BASE/workflows/system/events.transitions, (t) => !['ignored'].includes(t.name))" } ], "children": { "$ref": "$BASE/workflows/system/events.children", …its own children } }`.
